title: Brew & Chew Close Out Event
descriptionHtml:
Last month we opened ballots for our Brew & Chew Ranked Choice Voting social event at Strike Brewing in San Jose. We will be closing ballots and announcing the winners at Strike on Friday, July 25! Come join us to socialize with comrades, hear the election results, and spread the word about ranked choice voting in our community. Ballots remain open until this final event, so be sure to head to Strike Brewing and bring your friends in the interim to get higher turnout. There is also a ‘ballot box’ at Strike where you can share reasons why you support ranked choice voting. When we announce the winners, we will randomly choose one of the contributors and they will be awarded a $100 gift card. You have to be present when the winners are called to be eligible for the gift card.

We invite you to Strike Brewing on July 25 at 6 pm.

RSVP here: https://www.mobilize.us/calrcv/event/815416/

title: SJPJC Garden Day
descriptionHtml:
The Silicon Valley DSA Mutual Aid Working group, in association with San Jose Food Not Bombs and South Bay Mutual Aid, is hosting a garden and build day this Saturday at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center (SJPJC)! We will be moving soil, planting plants, garden maintenance, and finishing the drip irrigation! Be sure to bring gloves, a hat, earplugs, sunglasses, and sunscreen! If you have tools like a shovel, they will be needed!

Location Details
San Jose Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Wheelchair Accessibility

We will mostly be working outside the Center itself in the garden. To enter the Center itself: There is a wheelchair lift to access the 1st floor behind the building past the gate. Please ring the doorbell next to the lift for assistance.

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

title: No Appetite for Apartheid Campaign for Palestine (Santa Clara)
descriptionHtml:
Come join the International Solidarity Working Group and participate in outreach as part of the No Appetite for Apartheid campaign that we are running locally in Santa Clara! This event will be handing out flyers at the MCA Mosque in Santa Clara during Jummah prayer.

No Appetite for Apartheid is a national campaign that follows the principles of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement to reduce US support for Israeli apartheid and genocide against Palestinians. The campaign urges local small businesses to stop carrying Israeli food products and educates community members about supporting Palestine by boycotting Israeli products, a time-tested consumer tactic used against states perpetrating injustice.

If you’re interested in attending this event, join our Google Group here to get in contact with the organizers!
Click “Ask to join group” if you have a Gmail account, or “Contact owners and managers” if you do not. You can also reach out to #wg-international-solidarity on our Slack.

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

title: Redwood City No Appetite for Apartheid Canvass
descriptionHtml:
Come join the International Solidarity Working Group and participate in our first No Appetite for Apartheid canvass in Redwood City!

No Appetite for Apartheid is a national campaign that follows the principles of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement to reduce US support for Israeli apartheid and genocide against Palestinians. The campaign urges local small businesses to stop carrying Israeli food products and educates community members about supporting Palestine by boycotting Israeli products, a time-tested consumer tactic used against states perpetrating injustice. During our canvass, we’ll be visiting businesses in Redwood City and asking them to drop Israeli food products as well as to put up a flyer showing the community their support for Palestinians.

If you’re interested in attending this event and want to know the location, join our Google Group here to get in contact with the organizers! Click “Ask to join group” if you have a Gmail account, or “Contact owners and managers” if you do not. You can also reach out to #wg-international-solidarity on our Slack.

title: South Bay Labor Council movie screening, “American Agitators.”
descriptionHtml:
The Labor WG of Silicon Valley DSA invites all labor-interested folks to join us in attending the screening of “American Agitators,” which won the Best Documentary award at Cinequest in San Jose this year! In the words of one review, it “chronicles the life and teachings of Fred Ross, Sr., who understood that inequality leads to injustice. Inspiring a new generation of activists to organize for systemic change, the film shows how collective action can combat racism, bigotry, and greed.”

Free admission.

Come join your Labor WG comrades in solidarity with the South Bay Labor Council, as we build a stronger relationship between our chapter and organized labor.

And stay tuned for a later screening, by the Labor Working Group, of “Union,” the documentary of the fight for the Amazon Labor Union. That will happen late in September, or early October.

Hope to see you on Friday the 5th of September! Help spread the word.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San Jose No Appetite for Apartheid
descriptionHtml:
Come join the International Solidarity Working Group and participate in a No Appetite for Apartheid canvass in San Jose! We’ll be meeting in front of San Jose City Hall.

No Appetite for Apartheid is a national campaign that follows the principles of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement to reduce US support for Israeli apartheid and genocide against Palestinians. The campaign urges local small businesses to stop carrying Israeli food products and educates community members about supporting Palestine by boycotting Israeli products, a time-tested consumer tactic used against states perpetrating injustice. During our canvass, we’ll be visiting businesses in San Jose and asking them to drop Israeli food products as well as to put up a flyer showing the community their support for Palestinians.

If you’re interested in attending this event and want to know more details, join our Google Group here to get in contact with the organizers! Click “Ask to join group” if you have a Gmail account, or “Contact owners and managers” if you do not. You can also reach out to #wg-international-solidarity on our Slack.

descriptionHtml:

title: Pack the Court for the Stanford 11!
descriptionHtml:
[URGENT ACTION] ‼️PACK THE COURT‼️ for the Stanford 11 – this Monday, Oct 6th @ 8:15am, join us at San Jose Hall of Justice, Department 24 -to support student protestors’ rights to free speech! – Court begins at 8:30AM.

In a highly unusual and backhanded move, Santa Clara County’s DA Rosen & DDA Baker secured a grand jury indictment for 11 defendants in the case against the Stanford 12. The Indictment has side-stepped the preliminary hearing phase, taking court proceedings out of the public sphere as part of a broader authoritarian effort to criminalize protest and free speech. Grand juries are secretive and repressive processes held without the knowledge of defendants or their lawyers, entirely presided over by the District Attorney. Meanwhile Stanford continues to bow to the Trump administration in a new era of fascist political repression, and continues to be complicit in Israel’s crimes of genocide and apartheid.

As the Stanford 11 remain firm in their continued opposition to the ongoing genocide and catastrophic famine in Gaza, we the student and broader community, re-affirm our support for students and the civil right to free speech and protest. PACK THE COURT for the Stanford 11!  Show the DA that the community is watching, and that he cannot take this case out of the public eye!

STANFORD DIVEST! WE WILL NOT STOP WE WILL NOT REST! UNTIL PALESTINE IS FREE! UNTIL PALESTINE IS FREE! 🔻

Sign the petition to support & for further case updates: bit.ly/stanford11Petition

The 11 defendants will be re-arraigned on docket #C251537
🗓️Monday 10/6 @ 8:30am
📍 Dept. 24 of the San Jose Hall of Justice. 190-200 W Hedding St, San Jose, CA 95110

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

descriptionHtml:
Curious about socialism but don’t know where to start? In need of some comradely time to unwind? Want to connect with other local comrades and build community? Join us for our October Last Friday Social!

This month, we will be taking a 90 minute guided tour to learn about the history of activism and progressivism in San José. It begins at the San José Peace & Justice Center and ends near city hall.

After the tour, we will meet nearby to socialize, eat, and drink at Peanuts Deluxe Cafe, a business that recently changed ownership and became a co-op. Peanuts will also be hosting open mic night, so feel free to prepare something if you want to participate!

Hope you can make it! Feel free to bring friends, family, or anyone else who is interested.

  1. SJ Peace & Justice Center
  2. SJSU Chavez Arch

  4. Internment Monument (South Second Street)
  5. Ernesto Galarza Table (Market Street)
  6. Former CPUSA Headquarters (Post Street)
  7. Sarah Knox-Goodrich Building (First Street)

*If you drive, DO NOT park in the Grocery Outlet parking lot. Your car will get towed.*

  • They do serve food and drinks (no peanuts)

title: DSA 101
descriptionHtml:
At DSA, we believe a better world is possible. But the only way it can happen is if we organize together as members of the working class to restructure society based on human needs. DSA is the largest socialist organization in the United States, but we have to grow even larger to change our society. One barrier to growth is lack of knowledge about socialism in general and DSA as an organization specifically.

What is socialism? How can we achieve it? What projects does Silicon Valley DSA work on? How is our chapter structured to do work? How can I get involved? We are running a DSA 101 event where we will answer these questions and any others that you bring. This event is open to the public, and we encourage non-members to get involved and come with any questions.

The event will be held at SEIU 521 Union Hall on Saturday October 25 at 12:15-1 PM, right before our monthly General Chapter Meeting.

A hybrid Zoom option is available. Register at this link: https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/Dkzcam-2SjerPLuBlEGQOQ

title: Beyond Survival: Disability, Resilience and Justice
descriptionHtml:
Join the San Jose Peace and Justice Center and partners in hosting a diverse panel discussion exploring what it means to grieve the self we used to be and how to nurture resilience in the face of that loss. Together, we will reflect on the complexities of self- grief, honor the emotions that come with change, and explore ways to imagine hope, identity, and purpose.

How does this go beyond the individual? How, as a community, can we support those of us with a disability?

This event is co-sponsored by Silicon Valley DSA!

title: San Jose No Appetite for Apartheid Canvass
descriptionHtml:
Come join the International Solidarity Working Group and participate in a No Appetite for Apartheid canvass in San Jose! We’ll be meeting in front of San Jose City Hall.

No Appetite for Apartheid is a national campaign that follows the principles of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement to reduce US support for Israeli apartheid and genocide against Palestinians. The campaign urges local small businesses to stop carrying Israeli food products and educates community members about supporting Palestine by boycotting Israeli products, a time-tested consumer tactic used against states perpetrating injustice. During our canvass, we’ll be visiting businesses in San Jose and asking them to drop Israeli food products as well as to put up a flyer showing the community their support for Palestinians.

If you’re interested in attending this event and want to know more details, join our Google Group here to get in contact with the organizers! Click “Ask to join group” if you have a Gmail account, or “Contact owners and managers” if you do not. You can also reach out to #wg-international-solidarity on our Slack.

title: Phone Zap for Stanford 11
descriptionHtml:
In June 2024, students, alumni, and one student reporter were arrested at a sit-in of the office of Stanford University’s president in protest of Stanford’s complicity with Israel’s genocide in Palestine. In Santa Clara County, the District Attorney Jeff Rosen has chosen to charge these protesters against genocide with felonies, and 11 Stanford community members have been indicted on two grand jury charges, making them the first out of thousands of protesters across the nation in the past two years to go to felony trial over their pro-Palestinian activism.

The next court date for the Stanford 11 is November 17, where trial proceedings are set to be scheduled and assigned. Therefore, Silicon Valley DSA’s international solidarity working group is standing in solidarity with the Stanford 11 by holding a weekly phone zap among our members to call Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen, Stanford University’s President Levin, and Representative Ro Khanna to pressure them to drop these unprecedented charges against the Stanford 11! Join us by registering for the phone zap here.

If you can’t join us, you can also call and email using Stanford SJP’s action toolkit.

Please join us as we support the on-going strike wave of Starbucks baristas; join us as we support local teachers’ associations, and domestic workers, and others, struggling for dignity and a fair contract; join us as we push ourselves and our chapter into workplace organizing; and join us as we build a union caucus within Silicon Valley DSA, and strengthen our presence in the South Bay Labor Coalition.

title: Labor Movie Night “Partners” Ultra-topical!
descriptionHtml:
Join us on Thursday evening, December 4th at 7 pm, at the SEIU-521 Hall, 2302 Zanker Road, for a screening of “Partners.” This documentary screening couldn’t be more timely, given that the Starbucks Workers United-led strike wave has reached San José!

The full title of the film: “Partners: A Film About How Starbucks Baristas Started a Labor Revolution.” Yes, this is a Gen-Z led labor revolution! A union struggle breaking new ground in a gig-work dominated industry.

This screening will be special in several ways: we will have a SWU strike leader with us, to discuss and answer questions. We will have baristas and SWU staff joining us from the area, including Santa Cruz, where the strikes began in California. And we will be able to build support right there and then, to support the on-going strikes in San José.

Food and drink will also be on hand. Make plans to attend, and help spread the word!

title: DSA 101
descriptionHtml:
At DSA, we believe a better world is possible. But the only way this can happen is if we organize together as members of the working class to restructure society based on human needs. DSA is the largest socialist organization in the United States, but we have to grow even larger to change our society. One barrier to growth is lack of knowledge about socialism in general and DSA as an organization specifically.

What is socialism? How can we achieve it? What projects does Silicon Valley DSA work on? How is our chapter structured to do work? How can I get involved? We are running a DSA 101 event where we will answer these questions and any others that you bring. This event is open to the public, and we encourage non-members to get involved and come with any questions.

The event will be held at SEIU 521 Union Hall on Saturday, December 5th from 6:30PM-7:30 PM.

Join us for an after-101 social! Disclosed after the meeting.

Register for the Zoom: https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/u1Z0bjUvTSia0y6TXtcxLA

title: Pack City Hall for Summerwind Tenant Union
descriptionHtml:
In November, we advocated to the San Jose Code Enforcement Appeals Board with the tenants at Summerwind Apartments in East San Jose, who have been in a battle against their landlords due to their poor living conditions, including issues with pests and mold.

At the November meeting, code enforcement promised action – and updates – but no change occurred for these residents. So, we’re returning to hold code enforcement to their word.

Join us on Thursday, December 11 at 6:30 pm to support the Summerwind Tenant Union and call for action for the landlords’ code violations. The hearing will take place in the Council Chambers at San Jose City Hall (200 E. Santa Clara Street). Be there and help us show up for tenants’ rights!

Location details:
San  Jose City Hall
200 E Santa Clara St.
San Jose, CA 95113

Meeting location:
We will gather outside of chambers. The meeting will be held in council chambers, but not through the traditional entrance for council meetings. The entrance will be on the first/ground floor at the back of the rotunda (south side, think of Santa Clara Street being the “front.”) Follow the hallway and a placard will indicate council chambers. A map exists below with arrows indicating entrance.

Meeting notes:

  • Talking points are available here.
  • This item is not on the regular agenda. We will be giving public comment at the end of the meeting (Agenda Item 9)
  • Giving public comment: Upon arrival, fill out a (pink?) card which will be at the front of the room or on the wooden guard in front of the seating area.

Parking:
City Hall garage will be closed. Park in the Fourth Street garage, 44 S. Fourth St. and San Fernando, which offers the first 90 minutes free (the meeting will likely run longer than 90 minutes). Cost: $1.00 every 20 minutes, $20 max; $5.00 after 6:00 p.m., weekdays. Please see photo at bottom of this post for walking directions from garage to chambers.

Transit:
Light rail service is available to Santa Clara and First / Second Streets. Bus Lines: 22, 63, 64, 65

We may be able to connect you with carpooling. Please contact us at info@siliconvalleydsa.org.

Accessibility:

  • The general seating area is accessed by stairs. We assume additional seating is available in accordance with ADA guidelines.
  • There will be ample room for distancing, if desired – chambers seat 300+ and less than 50 attendees were present at the 11/13 meeting (~20 of them being with our group).
  • It is not necessary to remain in chambers the full duration of the meeting. Personal breaks can be taken at any time simply by leaving through the entrance. No signin/out etc. is required.
  • Food and drink is prohibited in chambers but can be consumed outside. (Water is likely fine).
  • Closed captioning is often provided without request.
  • The meeting will take place in English, however we expect Spanish translators to be available.

Additional information about the San Jose Appeals Hearing Board is here.
excerpt: Join us at the San Jose Code Enforcement Appeals Board Hearing to support the Summerwind Tenant Union and call for action for the landlords’ code violations.

title: Phone Zap for Stanford 11
descriptionHtml:
In June 2024, students, alumni, and one student reporter were arrested at a sit-in of the office of Stanford University’s president in protest of Stanford’s complicity with Israel’s genocide in Palestine. In Santa Clara County, the District Attorney Jeff Rosen has chosen to charge these protesters against genocide with felonies, and 11 Stanford student protesters have been indicted on two grand jury charges, making them the first out of thousands of protesters across the nation in the past two years to go to felony trial over their pro-Palestinian activism.

The next court date for the Stanford 11 is November 17, where trial proceedings are set to be scheduled and assigned. Therefore, Silicon Valley DSA’s international solidarity working group is standing in solidarity with the Stanford 11 by holding a weekly phone zap among our members to call Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen, Stanford University’s President Levin, and Representative Ro Khanna to pressure them to drop these unprecedented charges against the Stanford 11! Join us by registering for the phone zap here.

If you can’t join us, you can also call and email using Stanford SJP’s action toolkit.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

Location Details
San José Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

title: SJPJC Garden Day
descriptionHtml:
The Silicon Valley DSA Mutual Aid Working group, in association with San Jose Food Not Bombs and South Bay Mutual Aid, is hosting a garden and build day this Saturday at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center (SJPJC)! We will be moving soil, planting plants, garden maintenance, and finishing the drip irrigation! Be sure to bring gloves, a hat, earplugs, sunglasses, and sunscreen! If you have tools like a shovel, they will be needed!

Location Details
San Jose Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Wheelchair Accessibility

We will mostly be working outside the Center itself in the garden. To enter the Center itself: There is a wheelchair lift to access the 1st floor behind the building past the gate. Please ring the doorbell next to the lift for assistance.

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: Community Briefing: NO to the proposed Gilroy ICE facility
descriptionHtml:
ICE is trying to move to build a facility in South County — and our community is fighting back.

Although there is not definitive information about the future use for this land, our community will be vigilant and organized to ensure ICE can not expand deportation operations in the Bay at this site.

On May 22, join us for a community briefing to get the full picture: what we know, what’s at stake, and how we stop it. This is your chance to hear directly from community leaders, ask questions, and plug into the campaign.

This facility would threaten the safety and well being of immigrant families across the entire region. Research has consistently shown that communities located near ICE detention centers experience increased enforcement activity and higher rates of arrests—a pattern that puts immigrant families, mixed-status households, and entire neighborhoods at greater risk.

Santa Clara County is home to one of the largest immigrant populations in California. For years, county leaders and community organizations have fought to pass and defend strong sanctuary protections because they know that the safety of immigrant residents is inseparable from the safety and well being of the whole county. A new ICE detention center in Gilroy would be a direct threat to everything those protections stand for.

Sign up here for a link to join: https://actionnetwork.org/events/community-briefing-no-to-the-proposed-gilroy-ice-facility

title: DSA 101
descriptionHtml:
Are you tired of a system that is rigged against the Working Class? Have you had enough frustration with the status quo, and want to do something about it?

At DSA, we believe a better world is possible. Join us to learn about the movement we are building, and how to create power for the only majority in this country, the Working Class!

What is Democratic Socialism? How does DSA work to achieve it? Which projects does Silicon Valley DSA work on? At our DSA 101 event, we will answer these questions and many others. This event is open to the public, so we encourage non-members come hear why we joined, and why we stuck around. Discover how we are helping the community, and how you can get involved to build a better world.

The event will be held at SEIU 521 Union Hall on Saturday, May 23rd from 12:00 to 1:00 PM.

Please RSVP HERE.

Join us after the DSA 101 for our monthly Chapter Meeting, which starts at 1:00PM. You can talk to members, get more questions answered, and see a meeting in action.

descriptionHtml:

We also have shorter options with less elevation gain if you want to come but would prefer something less strenuous! We’ll be meeting at 9:00am and beginning the Windy Hill Loop at 9:15am.
Please get in touch if you are interested in carpooling. Hope to see you there!

title: All Hands on Deck! Stand Against Flock in Palo Alto
descriptionHtml:
All Hands On Deck! Indivisible Palo Alto Plus and the Safety Over Surveillance Palo Alto Coalition are organizing one final targeted action in Palo Alto before the Council goes on Summer Recess. SV-DSA is a founding member of the SOS Coalition.

The plan is simple: Show up for pizza on the Plaza at 5pm and join us in Council Chambers during General Comments at 5:30pm. Two designated spokespeople from the coalition will urge the council to (1) cover Flock cameras while council researches Flock during the summer recess, and (2) cancel the city’s Flock contract, especially in light of federal plans to open two detention centers in the Bay Area. You do not need to be a Palo Alto resident and will not be asked to speak. Since the Council will not be able to take action, our goal is not to bombard the Council with public comments, but to provide them with a few parting remarks to consider during the break and demonstrate popular opposition to the cameras by mass mobilization.

More information can be found at https://www.mobilize.us/indivisible/event/971008/ and please RSVP so we know how much pizza to order.

We hope you’ll join us!

title: DSA 101
descriptionHtml:
Are you tired of a system that is rigged against the Working Class? Have you had enough frustration with the status quo, and want to do something about it?

At DSA, we believe a better world is possible. Join us to learn about the movement we are building, and how to create power for the only majority in this country, the Working Class!

What is Democratic Socialism? How does DSA work to achieve it? Which projects does Silicon Valley DSA work on? At our DSA 101 event, we will answer these questions and many others. This event is open to the public, so we encourage non-members come hear why we joined, and why we stuck around. Discover how we are helping the community, and how you can get involved to build a better world.

The event will be held at SEIU 521 Union Hall on Saturday, June 27th from 12:00 to 1:00 PM.

Please RSVP HERE.

Join us after the DSA 101 for our monthly Chapter Meeting, which starts at 1:00PM. You can talk to members, get more questions answered, and see a meeting in action.

To take part in Chapter decisions as a voting member, please sign up with National DSA at https://dsausa.org/join.

Parking

There is parking in the union hall parking lot.

Public Transportation

Bus: Brokaw & Rogers (VTA Line 60), 1st & Bonaventura (VTA Line 203)

title: Democracy Forum – Who’s Watching? Safeguarding Our Privacy
descriptionHtml:
Silicon Valley DSA is an active participant in opposing automated license plate readers and the expansion of the surveillance state in Santa Clara County. We are members of the Safety Over Surveillance (SOS) coalition that supports evidence-based approaches to promoting public safety and community needs over building a panopticon that erodes our democracy and civil liberties. Join us with Indivisible Palo Alto + and the SOS coalition for a forum on democracy and mass surveillance on Sunday, June 28 from 3-5:30 pm at the First Presbyterian Church in Palo Alto (1140 Cowper St.).

Register for the event here: https://www.mobilize.us/ipaplus/event/961311/

Event description from webpage:

About this event

Democracy cannot flourish when privacy is under threat.

Rulers have spied on their subjects since time immemorial. The less democratic the government, the greater the impulse to monitor its population.

Our founders established safeguards against this behavior—most notably, the Fourth Amendment to the Constitution. However, two trends are coalescing to fuel a new and dangerous era of American mass surveillance:

  1. The rise of Big Tech and digital surveillance capacities that reach far beyond anything that James Madison could have imagined
  2. A federal government that, instead of upholding the right to privacy, seeks to weaponize technology to consolidate its power and to marginalize or prosecute political rivals

Mass surveillance of American citizens has arrived at federal and local levels. It has the potential to radically alter the lives of every American—and to radically shape the future of our democracy.

Participants in this session of Democracy Forum will explore the “brave new world” of mass surveillance, its impact on our everyday lives, and its implications for our democracy. They will also learn about ways to counter mass surveillance and to protect their privacy.

PROGRAM

Nationally recognized experts will discuss these critical developments:

  • The latest “advances” in surveillance technology and deployment
  • The actions of the Trump administration to promote mass surveillance
  • The growing alliance of Big Government and Big Tech
  • The spread of surveillance technology in our communities
  • The proliferation of apps on our personal devices (including mobile phones and personal computers) that monitor our actions and speech, both online and offline
  • The increasing adoption of mass surveillance methods by ICE and other agencies
  • The use of mass surveillance technologies to target, harass, and prosecute people of color and vulnerable populations

Following a plenary session featuring expert panel, there will be a series of breakout sessions:

  • Digital Privacy
  • Cameras on Our Streets: Automated License Plate Readers and Us
  • Mass Surveillance and Racial Justice
  • Mass Surveillance and Dissent
  • Legal Protections and Remedies: What Is Working and What Has Failed

Participants will leave with deepened knowledge and understanding of these topics:

  • How mass surveillance affects our lives—on our personal devices and in our local communities
  • How mass surveillance intersects or conflicts with democracy, privacy, and civil liberties
  • How the alliance of Big Government and Big Tech threatens constitutional and legal privacy protections
  • How organized citizens can work to protect public safety and civil liberties

SPEAKERS

A wide range of experts on mass surveillance and civil liberties will lead the plenary and breakout sessions. Here are the speakers confirmed thus far:

Cindy Cohn has led the Electronic Frontier Foundation—an organization that defends civil liberties in the digital age—for the past thirty years. A leading advocate against government overreach, she has spearheaded landmark legal battles to limit mass surveillance and to protect constitutional rights against threats posed by modern technology.

Cyrus Farivar is an award-winning journalist and author whose work has focused on technology policy, surveillance law, and consumer privacy. He has covered tech policy for several media outlets, including Ars Technica, Forbes, and NBC News. In addition, he has written two books, The Internet of Elsewhere (2011) and Habeas Data (2018). In 2025, he joined Fire Aside, a startup that develops software for fire departments. He is based in Oakland.

Brian Hofer is the executive director of Secure Justice. He is also the architect of Oakland’s pioneering surveillance technology ordinance and the chair of its privacy advisory commission. A privacy advocate known for his work on local government oversight, he specializes in turning civil rights advocacy into enforceable policy that limits unwarranted state spying.

Reem Sulaiman is the senior campaigns director at Fight for the Future, a nonprofit digital rights group that focuses on internet freedom and anti-surveillance advocacy. Previously, she served as the U.S. advocacy lead for the Mozilla Foundation. Based in Oakland, she has deep experience in local civic tech policy and served as an original member of the Oakland Privacy Advisory Commission

CONNECT. LEARN. ACT.

Who’s Watching? Safeguarding Our Privacy is the third presentation of Democracy Forum, a series of action-oriented events hosted by Indivisible Palo Alto Plus. Democracy Forum aims to provide a “deep dive” educational experience that will equip participants with the knowledge, skills, and tools that they need to preserve and strengthen the American democratic experiment.

title: ICE Out of Gilroy and Dublin–World Cup
descriptionHtml:
Join SVDSA and other anti-ICE coalition members, like Bay Resistance, as we demand that ICE leave the place we call home, and leave our neighbors in peace.

The federal government plans to build ICE detention centers in Gilroy and Dublin. If this happens, operations in the bay area will increase and our neighbors will be put at risk. We must speak out against these dangerous and cruel detention centers. We must demand that ICE leaves and stays out of the Bay Area. We must demand that ICE be abolished.

 

This event will start at 3PM and we will meet at Lick Mill Station (2221 Tasman Drive, Santa Clara 95054). This location is accessible from VTA’s green and orange lines.

Stay tuned to this page for more information.

descriptionHtml:
Ever wondered how to form a union at work? Want to organize your workplace but don’t know where to start?

Join us for an upcoming Fundamentals of Workplace Organizing training to hear from organizers and people like you who want to organize their workplaces! In small discussion groups with participants across Silicon Valley, you’ll learn how to build a campaign, take collective action, and escalate. Critical to any organizing effort is a campaign based on the key issues that targets decision-makers and consistently escalates action.

Following the training, all attendees are invited to join us for a social at Peanuts Deluxe Cafe until 10pm! Need a ride there? Ask one of organizers!

title: Forum on ICE Facility, Data Center, and Mass Surveillance July 19
descriptionHtml:
Silicon Valley DSA has endorsed and is participating in a forum hosted by our allies in Bay Resistance (Mountain View Pod) on Sunday July 19 at 3 pm. The event will be held in the Maple Room of the Mountain View Community Center at 201 S Rengstorff Ave.

The event will consist of a panel discussion bringing together three experienced local organizers. One member is active in the fight against the ICE processing facility being illegally constructed in Gilroy. One member is active fighting against the data center planned for South County. One member is active in the fight against mass surveillance and automated license plate readers. The discussion will highlight the ties between these seemingly disparate topics and how residents of the Lower Peninsula can get involved in opposing the developments in South County.

Register to attend here: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScvC0ooztxuRjGnuzVbtZw3h6tme066um5SvSaRUpkLvw4OoQ/viewform

Description from Bay Resistance located at the registration link above:

The construction of detention centers and data centers across the US represent some of the largest construction efforts in recent times. Both have been heavily protested, and while on the surface seem like distinct efforts, the artificial intelligence boom and the growth of surveillance and the deportation pipeline are deeply interrelated. In Gilroy, we have an example of both being constructed at this very moment. Hear from local activists in Gilroy about the build out of the new data center and detention center in their community, the local organizing to protest them, and how these projects affect immigrants and all working people in the area.

La construcción de centros de detención y centros de datos en todo Estados Unidos representa algunos de los proyectos de construcción más grandes de los últimos tiempos. Ambos han sido objeto de fuertes protestas y, aunque a primera vista parecen iniciativas distintas, el auge de la inteligencia artificial, el crecimiento de la vigilancia y el sistema de deportaciones están profundamente interrelacionados. En Gilroy, tenemos un ejemplo de la construcción simultánea de ambos tipos de instalaciones. Escuche a activistas locales de Gilroy hablar sobre la construcción del nuevo centro de datos y del centro de detención en su comunidad, la organización local para protestar contra ellos y cómo estos proyectos afectan a los inmigrantes y a todos los trabajadores de la zona.

descriptionHtml:

title: DSA 101
descriptionHtml:
Are you tired of a system that is rigged against the Working Class? Have you had enough frustration with the status quo, and want to do something about it?

At DSA, we believe a better world is possible. Join us to learn about the movement we are building, and how to create power for the only majority in this country, the Working Class!

What is Democratic Socialism? How does DSA work to achieve it? Which projects does Silicon Valley DSA work on? At our DSA 101 event, we will answer these questions and many others. This event is open to the public, so we encourage non-members come hear why we joined, and why we stuck around. Discover how we are helping the community, and how you can get involved to build a better world.

The event will be held at SEIU 521 Union Hall on Saturday, August 1st from 12:00 to 1:00 PM.

Please RSVP HERE.

Join us after the DSA 101 for our monthly Chapter Meeting, which starts at 1:00PM. You can talk to members, get more questions answered, and see a meeting in action.

To take part in Chapter decisions as a voting member, please sign up with National DSA at https://dsausa.org/join.

Parking

There is parking in the union hall parking lot.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

descriptionHtml:

title: SJPJC Garden Day
descriptionHtml:
The Silicon Valley DSA Mutual Aid Working group, in association with San Jose Food Not Bombs and South Bay Mutual Aid, is hosting a garden and build day this Saturday at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center (SJPJC)! We will be moving soil, planting plants, garden maintenance, and finishing the drip irrigation! Be sure to bring gloves, a hat, earplugs, sunglasses, and sunscreen! If you have tools like a shovel, they will be needed!

Location Details
San Jose Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Wheelchair Accessibility

We will mostly be working outside the Center itself in the garden. To enter the Center itself: There is a wheelchair lift to access the 1st floor behind the building past the gate. Please ring the doorbell next to the lift for assistance.

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

descriptionHtml:
Join the mutual aid working group to help support community-based efforts in the South Bay! No experience is required and everyone has something to contribute! We will be meeting at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center and a zoom link is available for those who cannot join in person.

We will discuss:

– Our current projects such as the San Jose Free Store, our gardens at Grateful Garden and the San Jose Peace and Justice Center, as well as a brake light clinic/repair cafe!

– Supporting South Bay Mutual Aid (SBMA) as one of their coalition members. Sign up to volunteer with SBMA here: https://southbaymutualaid.org/volunteermulti

This meeting will be conducted online.

title: August Leadership Retreat
descriptionHtml: Silicon Valley DSA holds quarterly leadership retreats so we can take a big picture view of our ongoing organizing work. We also work to develop member leaders and strategize about building coalitions with other local groups aligned with our goals and values. The retreat is open to all member leaders, and any members who are interested in stepping up into a larger role in the organization are encouraged to attend. We will hold a retreat at the SEIU 521 Union Hall. Come join us to help set the direction of the organization and work out strategies to empower our members to develop as leaders in SV DSA and the larger community.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: SJPJC Garden Day
descriptionHtml:
The Silicon Valley DSA Mutual Aid Working group, in association with San Jose Food Not Bombs and South Bay Mutual Aid, is hosting a garden and build day this Saturday at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center (SJPJC)! We will be moving soil, planting plants, garden maintenance, and finishing the drip irrigation! Be sure to bring gloves, a hat, earplugs, sunglasses, and sunscreen! If you have tools like a shovel, they will be needed!

Location Details
San Jose Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Wheelchair Accessibility

We will mostly be working outside the Center itself in the garden. To enter the Center itself: There is a wheelchair lift to access the 1st floor behind the building past the gate. Please ring the doorbell next to the lift for assistance.

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

title: SJPJC Garden Day
descriptionHtml:
The Silicon Valley DSA Mutual Aid Working group, in association with San Jose Food Not Bombs and South Bay Mutual Aid, is hosting a garden and build day this Saturday at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center (SJPJC)! We will be moving soil, planting plants, garden maintenance, and finishing the drip irrigation! Be sure to bring gloves, a hat, earplugs, sunglasses, and sunscreen! If you have tools like a shovel, they will be needed!

Location Details
San Jose Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Wheelchair Accessibility

We will mostly be working outside the Center itself in the garden. To enter the Center itself: There is a wheelchair lift to access the 1st floor behind the building past the gate. Please ring the doorbell next to the lift for assistance.

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

descriptionHtml:

We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

title: San Jose Clothing Swap
descriptionHtml:
SJ Clothing Swap is mutual aid for our community through clothing and fabric, with an emphasis on sustainability, queer expression, intersectional community care, accessibility, and community organizing. We’re focused on:

– Quality clothes for all
– Being a safe space for exploring your style and gender expression
– Building local community and making new friends
– Combating fast fashion, clothing overproduction & overconsumption, and textile waste (keeping clothes out of landfills)

We want to help you clear your closet of clothes, shoes and accessories that you don’t wear, and take home amazing new styles for free!  We stop taking donations at 3:30 PM!

title: San José Free Store
descriptionHtml:
Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

title: Mutual Aid Working Group Meeting
descriptionHtml:
Join the mutual aid working group to help support community-based efforts in the South Bay! No experience is required and everyone has something to contribute! We will be meeting at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center and a zoom link is available for those who cannot join in person.

title: SJPJC Garden Day
descriptionHtml:
The Silicon Valley DSA Mutual Aid Working group, in association with San Jose Food Not Bombs and South Bay Mutual Aid, is hosting a garden and build day this Saturday at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center (SJPJC)! We will be moving soil, planting plants, garden maintenance, and finishing the drip irrigation! Be sure to bring gloves, a hat, earplugs, sunglasses, and sunscreen! If you have tools like a shovel, they will be needed!

Location Details
San Jose Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Wheelchair Accessibility

We will mostly be working outside the Center itself in the garden. To enter the Center itself: There is a wheelchair lift to access the 1st floor behind the building past the gate. Please ring the doorbell next to the lift for assistance.

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

Join Silicon Valley DSA, South Bay Mutual Aid, Food Not Bombs San José, San José Clothing Swap, and Art Pocket SJ, for a really really free goods event in the San José Peace and Justice Center parking lot. We’ll have cleaning supplies, clothes, fresh produce, fire preparedness kits, menstrual products, zines, and more available so that people can take what they need, for free.

Set up begins at 2 to 2:30 PM.  The Free Store will run from 3:30 to 6:00 PM and clean up will go from 6-7 PM~.  Please wear a mask to prevent the spread of respiratory diseases.

Feel free to bring and leave items you want to donate, but don’t bring more than 50 pounds of items, or items that won’t fit into a 2×2 box.

We look forward to seeing you!

Location Details
San José Peace & Justice Center Parking Lot
48 S. 7th Street
San Jose CA 95112

Parking

There is street parking and parking garages close by on 4th street. Do not park at the Grocery Outlet they will tow your car.

Public Transportation

Bus: 7th & Santa Clara (Rapid 523, 64), San Carlos / 7th (22, 23, 66), San Fernando & 7th (72,73)

Light Rail: Santa Clara Station – Blue and Green Line

Train: San Jose Diridon Station – take Rapid 500 to Santa Clara / 6th or 22 to San Carlos / 7th

Guidelines

For anyone entering the Center, it is recommended that you wear a mask. Thank you!

title: Mutual Aid Working Group Meeting
descriptionHtml:
Join the mutual aid working group to help support community-based efforts in the South Bay! No experience is required and everyone has something to contribute! We will be meeting at the San Jose Peace and Justice Center and a zoom link is available for those who cannot join in person.

We will discuss:

– Our current projects such as the San Jose Free Store, our gardens at Grateful Garden and the San Jose Peace and Justice Center, as well as a brake light clinic/repair cafe!

– Supporting South Bay Mutual Aid (SBMA) as one of their coalition members. Sign up to volunteer with SBMA here: https://southbaymutualaid.org/volunteermulti

This meeting will be conducted online.

Register Here for Zoom: https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/zJSg9nsyTrWrXQ-_uOptAQ
